title: Cowboy Breakfast Skillet
subtitle: Smoky beans, crispy potatoes, and eggs in one cast-iron pan.
description: Black beans, peppers, potatoes, and eggs with cheddar in cast iron — Southwest cowboy breakfast that fills the hall.

steps.title: Par-cook potatoes
steps.instruction: Microwave diced potatoes with water until just tender, drain, and pat dry. This shortens cast-iron time and guarantees creamy centers with crisp edges.

steps.title: Brown chorizo and veg
steps.instruction: In a large cast iron over medium-high, cook chorizo until rendered. Add onion and jalapeño; cook until softened. Fold in potatoes and chili powder until edges crisp.

steps.title: Add beans
steps.instruction: Stir in ranch beans with a splash of their liquid for saucy consistency. Simmer 3 minutes until the bottom of the skillet looks lightly glazed, not soupy.

steps.title: Eggs and cheese
steps.instruction: Make wells in the mixture and crack eggs into each. Cover over medium-low heat until egg whites are fully set (165°F) and yolks are jammy. Scatter cheddar over the top and cover 60 seconds to melt.

steps.title: Serve from the pan
steps.instruction: Garnish with cilantro and serve straight from the skillet family-style, or scoop portions onto warm plates. Keep extra hot sauce at the line.

stationWorkflow: Use two cast-iron skillets if feeding more than eight—split potatoes and chorizo evenly between pans.
Cover with a sheet pan lid if your skillet lacks a cover—steam sets egg whites faster on a loud morning.
Serve beans-on-the-bottom portions first; the top stays crisp longest for second-pass eaters.
cleanupNotes: Deglaze cast iron with hot water while warm, then scrape—bean sugars stick if left overnight.
Wipe jalapeño boards and knives immediately and wash hands before touching faces or eyes.
leftovers: Reheat in cast iron over medium with a lid, adding a splash of water to loosen beans before eggs re-crisp.
Mash leftovers into breakfast burrito filling with extra cheese and hot sauce for handheld service.
